name: Permutations nP2
description: Counts the number of ordered arrangements of 2 items chosen from n distinct items, equal to n*(n-1). Order matters, so picking A then B differs from B then A.
notes: n must be an integer of at least 2; otherwise the count is not meaningful. Items are assumed distinct and selected without replacement.

name: Permutations nP3
description: Counts the number of ordered arrangements of 3 items chosen from n distinct items, equal to n*(n-1)*(n-2). Each different order of the same three items is counted separately.
notes: n must be an integer of at least 3. Items are distinct and chosen without replacement; order is significant.

name: Combinations nC2
description: Counts the number of unordered pairs that can be chosen from n distinct items, equal to n*(n-1)/2. Unlike permutations, order does not matter, so pair A-B is the same as B-A.
notes: n must be an integer of at least 2. Items are distinct and selected without replacement; the result is always a whole number.

name: Combinations nC3
description: Counts the number of unordered triples that can be chosen from n distinct items, equal to n*(n-1)*(n-2)/6. Order within a group of three is ignored.
notes: n must be an integer of at least 3. Items are distinct and chosen without replacement; the division by 6 removes the 3! orderings of each triple.

name: Central Binomial Coefficient (Asymptotic)
description: Approximates the central binomial coefficient C(2n, n) as 4^n divided by sqrt(pi*n). It estimates the largest coefficient in the 2n-th row of Pascal's triangle for large n.
notes: This is an asymptotic approximation derived from Stirling's formula and slightly overestimates; accuracy improves as n grows. Here n is half the top index (2n choose n).

name: Catalan Number (Asymptotic)
description: Approximates the nth Catalan number as 4^n divided by ((n+1) times sqrt(pi*n)). Catalan numbers count many combinatorial structures such as balanced parentheses and binary trees.
notes: This is an asymptotic estimate that improves with larger n and is not exact; round to compare with the true integer Catalan number. Requires n at least 1.

name: Kummer's Theorem (p in a Binomial Coefficient)
expression: (digitsum(k, p) + digitsum(n - k, p) - digitsum(n, p)) / (p - 1)
description: Gives the exponent of p in C(n, k), which by Kummer's theorem equals the number of carries when adding k and n − k in base p.
notes: C(100, 50) is divisible by 3⁴ but not 3⁵.

name: Factorial n!
description: Multiplies the integers from 1 to n: the number of ways to arrange n distinct objects in a row.
notes: 20! = 2,432,902,008,176,640,000. Exact up to 18! with ordinary numbers and shown approximately up to 170!.

name: Combinations C(n, k)
description: Counts the ways to choose k items from n when order does not matter ("n choose k").
notes: C(49, 6) = 13,983,816, the number of possible tickets in a 6-from-49 lottery.

name: Permutations P(n, k)
description: Counts the ordered selections of k items from n: n!/(n − k)!.
notes: Gold, silver and bronze among 10 runners can be awarded in P(10, 3) = 720 ways.

name: Combinations with Repetition
description: Counts the multisets of size k drawn from n kinds when repetition is allowed ("stars and bars").
notes: Three scoops from five flavours can be chosen in C(7, 3) = 35 ways.

name: Multinomial Coefficient (Three Groups)
description: Counts the ways to split a + b + c distinct objects into labelled groups of sizes a, b and c.
notes: Also the number of distinct arrangements of a word with letter counts a, b, c. Here 9!/(2!3!4!) = 1260.

name: Arrangements of MISSISSIPPI
description: Counts the distinct orderings of the letters of MISSISSIPPI (1 M, 4 I, 4 S, 2 P), the classic multinomial example.
notes: The answer is 34,650.

name: Circular Permutations
description: Counts the ways to seat n people around a round table when rotations count as the same.
notes: If mirror images also count as the same (a necklace that can be flipped), divide by 2.

name: Necklaces with k Colours (Burnside)
expression: sum(d, 1, n, if(mod(n, d) == 0, phi(d) * k^(n / d), 0)) / n
description: Counts the distinct necklaces of n beads in k colours when rotations are identified, by Burnside's lemma: (1/n) Σ_{d|n} φ(d) k^(n/d).
notes: There are 14 binary necklaces of length 6.

name: Bracelets with k Colours
description: Counts necklaces that may also be turned over (bracelets): rotations and reflections are identified.
notes: There are 13 binary bracelets of length 6.

name: Derangements !n
description: Counts the permutations of n items in which nothing stays in its original place (the subfactorial !n).
notes: !10 = 1,334,961. The chance that a random permutation is a derangement tends to 1/e ≈ 36.8 %.

name: Secret Santa Failure Probability
description: Gives the chance that, when n people draw names at random, at least one person draws their own name.
notes: For large groups it approaches 1 − 1/e ≈ 63.2 %.

name: Rencontres Numbers D(n, k)
description: Counts the permutations of n items with exactly k fixed points.
notes: k = 0 gives the derangements. Summing over k gives n!.

name: Stirling Numbers of the Second Kind S(n, k)
description: Counts the ways to partition n labelled items into k non-empty unlabelled groups.

name: Stirling Numbers of the First Kind c(n, k)
description: Counts the permutations of n items with exactly k cycles (unsigned Stirling numbers of the first kind).

name: Bell Number B(n)
description: Counts all partitions of a set of n elements into non-empty groups.
notes: B(10) = 115,975. It is the sum of S(n, k) over k.

name: Ordered Bell (Fubini) Number
description: Counts the weak orderings of n items: the ways n competitors can finish a race when ties are allowed.
notes: Five runners can finish in 541 ways.

name: Surjections onto k Elements
description: Counts the onto functions from an n-element set to a k-element set — e.g. ways to hand n different jobs to k workers so that nobody is idle.
notes: Equivalent to inclusion–exclusion Σ (−1)^i C(k, i)(k − i)^n. Here 540.

name: Lah Numbers L(n, k)
description: Counts the ways to split n labelled items into k non-empty linearly ordered lists.

name: Integer Partitions p(n)
description: Counts the ways to write n as a sum of positive integers, ignoring order.
notes: p(100) = 190,569,292 (MacMahon's table, used by Hardy and Ramanujan).

name: Hardy–Ramanujan Partition Asymptotic
description: Approximates the partition number p(n) by e^(π√(2n/3)) / (4n√3) (Hardy and Ramanujan, 1918).
notes: Gives about 199,280,893 for n = 100, within 5 % of the exact 190,569,292; the full Rademacher series is exact.

name: Catalan Number C_n
description: The n-th Catalan number C(2n, n)/(n + 1): it counts balanced bracket strings, binary trees with n internal nodes, triangulations of an (n + 2)-gon and many more objects.

name: Triangulations of a Convex Polygon
description: Counts the ways to cut a convex n-gon into triangles with non-crossing diagonals: the Catalan number C_(n−2).
notes: An octagon has 132 triangulations.

name: Narayana Number N(n, k)
description: Counts the Dyck paths of semilength n with exactly k peaks (equivalently, bracket strings with k innermost pairs).
notes: Summing over k gives the Catalan number. N(5, 3) = 20.

name: Motzkin Number M_n
description: Counts the ways to draw non-crossing chords between n points on a circle (not every point needs a chord).

name: Large Schröder Number S_n
expression: sum(k, 0, n, binom(n + k, 2 * k) * catalan(k))
description: Counts lattice paths from (0, 0) to (n, n) with steps east, north and north-east that never rise above the diagonal.
notes: S₆ = 1806. Half of S_n counts the ways to bracket a sequence of n + 1 items, with two or more terms in each bracket.

name: Delannoy Number D(m, n)
expression: sum(k, 0, min(m, n), binom(m, k) * binom(n, k) * 2^k)
description: Counts the lattice paths from (0, 0) to (m, n) using steps east, north and north-east.
notes: The central value D(3, 3) = 63; Delannoy numbers also count alignments in sequence comparison.

name: Lattice Paths (Right and Up)
description: Counts the shortest grid routes from one corner to the opposite corner of an m × n grid.
notes: A 10 × 10 grid has C(20, 10) = 184,756 routes.

name: Ballot Theorem Probability
description: If A gets a votes and B gets b < a votes, counted in random order, this is the chance that A stays strictly ahead throughout the count (Bertrand's ballot theorem).
notes: With 60 against 40, A leads all the way with probability 0.2.

name: Eulerian Number A(n, m)
description: Counts the permutations of 1 … n with exactly m ascents (positions where the next number is larger).

name: Involutions (Telephone Numbers)
description: Counts the permutations that are their own inverse — equivalently, the ways n people can pair off for phone calls, with some left alone.

name: Perfect Matchings (2n Items)
description: Counts the ways to split 2n people into n unordered pairs: the double factorial (2n − 1)!!.
notes: 10 people can be paired in 945 ways.

name: Double Factorial n!!
description: Multiplies every other integer down from n: n(n − 2)(n − 4)…, ending at 1 or 2.

name: Superfactorial sf(n)
description: Multiplies the first n factorials: 1!·2!·…·n! (Sloane and Plouffe's superfactorial).

name: Hyperfactorial H(n)
description: Multiplies k^k for k from 1 to n.

name: Rising Factorial (Pochhammer)
description: Computes the rising factorial x(x + 1)…(x + n − 1), written (x)_n or x^(n).
notes: (3)_4 = 3·4·5·6 = 360. Works for non-integer x too.

name: Falling Factorial
description: Computes the falling factorial x(x − 1)…(x − n + 1).
notes: For integers it equals P(x, n); 7·6·5 = 210.

name: Subfactorial Approximation n!/e
description: The number of derangements equals n!/e rounded to the nearest integer, for every n ≥ 1.

name: Cayley's Formula (Labelled Trees)
description: Counts the spanning trees of the complete graph on n labelled vertices, i.e. the different trees on n labelled points.
notes: 6 labelled points can be joined into 6⁴ = 1296 trees.

name: Number of Labelled Graphs
description: Counts the simple graphs on n labelled vertices: each of the C(n, 2) possible edges is present or absent.
notes: 5 vertices give 2^10 = 1024 graphs.

name: Moser's Circle Problem (Regions)
description: Gives the greatest number of regions a circle is cut into by joining n points on it with chords.
notes: The pattern 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 breaks at 6 points, which give 31 regions, not 32.

name: Lazy Caterer's Sequence (Cuts of a Pancake)
description: Gives the maximum number of pieces a flat pancake can be cut into with n straight cuts.
notes: Ten cuts give at most 56 pieces.

name: Cake Numbers (Cuts of a Cube)
description: Gives the maximum number of pieces a solid cake can be cut into with n plane cuts.
notes: Ten cuts give at most 176 pieces.

name: Regions of the Plane by n Circles
description: Gives the maximum number of regions into which n circles divide the plane.
notes: Five circles give at most 22 regions; this is why a Venn diagram with circles stops working beyond three sets.

name: Inclusion–Exclusion for Three Sets
expression: a + b + c - ab - ac - bc + abc
description: Counts the elements of A ∪ B ∪ C from the sizes of the sets and of their intersections.
notes: Survey counts are a common use: students taking at least one of three subjects.

name: Pigeonhole Principle Minimum
description: If n items go into k boxes, some box must hold at least ⌈n/k⌉ of them.
notes: Among 367 people two must share a birthday (366 possible dates).

name: Frobenius Number (Two Coins)
description: For coprime a and b, gives the largest amount that cannot be paid with any combination of coins a and b (Sylvester, 1884).
notes: Requires gcd(a, b) = 1. With 5 and 7 you cannot pay 23, but every larger amount works.

name: Number of Non-representable Amounts (Two Coins)
description: For coprime a and b, counts the positive amounts that cannot be made from coins a and b (Sylvester).
notes: With 5 and 7 there are 12 such amounts: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 9, 11, 13, 16, 18, 23.

name: Josephus Problem (Every Second Person)
description: n people stand in a circle and every second one is eliminated; this gives the position of the survivor.
notes: Write n = 2^m + l with l < 2^m; the survivor is 2l + 1. For 41 people it is position 19.

name: Sum of a Row of Pascal's Triangle
description: Adds the binomial coefficients in row n of Pascal's triangle, which always gives 2^n (the number of subsets of an n-set).
notes: Row 10 sums to 1024.

name: Vandermonde's Identity
expression: sum(k, 0, r, binom(m, k) * binom(n, r - k))
description: Evaluates Σ C(m, k) C(n, r − k), which Vandermonde's identity says equals C(m + n, r): choosing r from two groups combined.

name: Hockey-Stick Identity
description: Adds C(i, r) down a diagonal of Pascal's triangle from i = r to n; the result is C(n + 1, r + 1).

name: Number of Subsets of Size at Most k
description: Counts the subsets of an n-element set with at most k elements.
notes: This is the Sauer–Shelah bound on shattered sets in learning theory; 176 for n = 10, k = 3.

name: Compositions of n into k Parts
description: Counts the ordered ways to write n as a sum of k positive integers.
notes: 10 can be written as an ordered sum of three positive parts in 36 ways.

name: Distributing Identical Balls into Distinct Boxes
description: Counts the ways to put n identical balls into k distinct boxes, empty boxes allowed.
notes: 10 balls into 4 boxes: C(13, 3) = 286 ways.

name: Total Number of Compositions
description: Counts all ordered ways to write n as a sum of positive integers (any number of parts).
notes: Each of the n − 1 gaps between n ones is either a plus sign or not, giving 2^(n−1) = 512 for n = 10.

name: Number of Binary Strings without Consecutive 1s
description: Counts the binary strings of length n with no two adjacent 1s, which is the Fibonacci number F(n + 2).
notes: There are 144 such strings of length 10.

name: Domino Tilings of a 2 × n Board
description: Counts the ways to tile a 2 × n rectangle with 1 × 2 dominoes.
notes: A 2 × 10 board has 89 tilings.

name: Domino Tilings of an m × n Board (Kasteleyn)
expression: round(prod(j, 1, ceil(m / 2), prod(k, 1, ceil(n / 2), 4 * cos(pi * j / (m + 1))^2 + 4 * cos(pi * k / (n + 1))^2)))
description: Counts the domino tilings of an m × n board with the Kasteleyn–Temperley–Fisher product formula.
notes: The 8 × 8 chessboard has 12,988,816 tilings. At least one of m, n must be even.

name: Sum of Products of Consecutive Pairs
description: Adds 1·2 + 2·3 + … + n(n + 1), which equals n(n + 1)(n + 2)/3.
notes: For n = 10 the sum is 440.

name: Number of Rectangles in an m × n Grid
description: Counts all rectangles (of any size) formed by the lines of an m × n grid: choose two horizontal and two vertical lines.
notes: A chessboard contains 1296 rectangles.

name: Non-attacking Rooks Placements
description: Counts the ways to place k rooks on an n × n board so that no two attack each other.
notes: Eight rooks on a chessboard: 8! = 40,320 ways.

name: Probability of a Full House in Poker
description: Gives the chance that a random 5-card hand from a 52-card deck is a full house (three of one rank and two of another).
notes: 3744 of the 2,598,960 hands, about 0.144 %.

name: Probability of a Flush in Poker
description: Gives the chance that a random 5-card hand is a flush (five cards of one suit, excluding straight and royal flushes).
notes: 5108 hands out of 2,598,960, about 0.197 %.

name: Lottery Jackpot Odds
description: Gives the chance of matching every number in a lottery that draws k of n main numbers and j of m bonus numbers.
notes: The defaults describe a 5-of-69 plus 1-of-26 game (as in US Powerball): 1 in 292,201,338.

name: Probability of Matching Exactly r Numbers (Lottery)
expression: binom(k, r) * binom(n - k, k - r) / binom(n, k)
description: Gives the hypergeometric chance of matching exactly r of the k drawn numbers in a k-from-n lottery.
notes: In 6-from-49, exactly three matches happen with probability about 1.77 %.

name: Probability of a Pair among n Dice
description: Gives the chance that at least two of n six-sided dice show the same face.
notes: With four dice it is about 72.2 %; with seven dice it is certain.

name: Probability of the Sum s with Two Dice
description: Gives the chance that two fair dice add up to s.
notes: 7 is the most likely total, with probability 1/6.

name: Coupon Collector's Expected Draws
description: Gives the expected number of random draws needed to collect all n equally likely coupons: n·H_n.
notes: Collecting all 50 cards takes about 225 draws on average.

name: Birthday Problem (Exact)
description: Gives the exact chance that at least two of n people share a birthday, assuming d equally likely days.
notes: With 23 people the chance first exceeds one half (about 50.7 %).

name: People Needed for a Shared Birthday
description: Estimates how many people are needed for at least one shared birthday with probability p, from the approximation n ≈ √(2d ln(1/(1 − p))).
notes: Gives 23 for a 50 % chance and 58 for 99 % (the exact answer is 57). The same estimate sizes hash collisions (the birthday attack).

name: Ramsey Number Upper Bound R(s, t)
description: Gives the Erdős–Szekeres upper bound C(s + t − 2, s − 1) for the Ramsey number R(s, t): any group that large contains s mutual friends or t mutual strangers.
notes: For R(4, 4) the bound is 20; the true value is 18. R(3, 3) = 6 is exactly the bound.

name: Erdős–Szekeres Monotone Subsequence Bound
description: Any sequence of more than (r − 1)(s − 1) distinct numbers contains an increasing subsequence of length r or a decreasing subsequence of length s; this gives that length.
notes: Every sequence of 17 distinct numbers has a monotone subsequence of length 5.

name: Handshake Lemma Edge Count
description: Gives the number of edges of a graph from the list of vertex degrees: the degrees always add up to twice the edge count.
notes: In particular, the number of odd-degree vertices is always even.

name: Euler Characteristic of a Polyhedron
description: Computes V − E + F, which is 2 for every convex polyhedron (Euler's polyhedron formula).
notes: A cube has 8 − 12 + 6 = 2. A torus-shaped polyhedron gives 0.

name: Edges of a Planar Graph (Upper Bound)
description: A simple planar graph with v ≥ 3 vertices has at most 3v − 6 edges.
notes: K₅ has 10 edges but the bound allows only 9, so K₅ is not planar.

name: Chromatic Polynomial of a Cycle
description: Counts the proper colourings of a cycle of n vertices with k colours (neighbours must differ).
notes: A pentagon can be properly 3-coloured in 30 ways.

name: Chromatic Polynomial of a Tree
description: Counts the proper k-colourings of any tree with n vertices: the first vertex has k choices, each further vertex k − 1.
notes: Any 5-vertex tree has 48 proper 3-colourings.

name: Number of Spanning Trees of a Complete Bipartite Graph
description: Counts the spanning trees of the complete bipartite graph K(m, n).
notes: K(3, 4) has 3³ × 4² = 432 spanning trees.

name: Hamiltonian Cycles in a Complete Graph
description: Counts the distinct round trips through n cities that visit each once, where direction does not matter — the search space of the travelling salesman problem.
notes: 10 cities give 181,440 tours; 20 cities already give about 6 × 10^16.

name: Rooted Labelled Trees
description: Counts the rooted trees on n labelled vertices: Cayley's n^(n−2) trees times n choices of root.
notes: 4 labelled vertices give 64 rooted trees.

name: Number of Binary Relations on an n-Set
description: Counts all binary relations on a set of n elements: every ordered pair is either related or not.
notes: A 3-element set has 2⁹ = 512 relations.

name: Number of Reflexive Relations
description: Counts the reflexive relations on an n-set: the diagonal pairs are fixed, the other n(n − 1) pairs are free.
notes: A 3-element set has 64 reflexive relations.

name: Number of Symmetric Relations
description: Counts the symmetric relations on an n-set: choose freely for the n diagonal pairs and the C(n, 2) unordered pairs.
notes: A 3-element set has 64 symmetric relations.

name: Number of Antisymmetric Relations
description: Counts the antisymmetric relations on an n-set: each diagonal pair is free and each unordered pair {a, b} has three options (neither, a→b, b→a).
notes: A 3-element set has 8 × 27 = 216 antisymmetric relations.

name: Sperner's Theorem (Largest Antichain)
description: Gives the largest number of subsets of an n-set such that none contains another (Sperner 1928).
notes: For n = 10 the maximum is C(10, 5) = 252, reached by taking all 5-element subsets.

name: Gaussian Binomial Coefficient [n, k]_q
description: Computes the q-binomial coefficient; for a prime power q it counts the k-dimensional subspaces of an n-dimensional vector space over the field with q elements.
notes: F₂⁴ has 35 two-dimensional subspaces. As q → 1 it tends to C(n, k).

name: Order of GL(n, q)
description: Counts the invertible n × n matrices over the field with q elements: the order of the general linear group.
notes: GL(3, 2) has 168 elements; GL(2, 2) has 6.

name: Catalan Triangle (Ballot Numbers)
description: Counts the sequences of n ones and k minus-ones whose partial sums never go negative (the Catalan triangle).
notes: For n = 4, k = 2 there are 9. The diagonal k = n gives the Catalan numbers.

name: Partitions into at Most Two Parts
description: Counts the partitions of n into at most two parts.

name: Partitions into at Most Three Parts
description: Counts the partitions of n into at most three parts, given by the nearest integer to (n + 3)²/12.
notes: For n = 10 the answer is 14.

name: Probability of Four of a Kind (5-Card Poker)
description: Gives the chance of being dealt four of a kind in five cards: 624 of the 2,598,960 hands.
notes: About 1 in 4165.

name: Probability of Three of a Kind (5-Card Poker)
description: Gives the chance of three of a kind (not a full house or four of a kind) in five cards.
notes: About 2.11 %.

name: Probability of Two Pair (5-Card Poker)
description: Gives the chance of exactly two pairs in five cards.
notes: About 4.75 %.

name: Probability of a Straight (5-Card Poker)
description: Gives the chance of five cards in sequence (not all one suit) in a five-card hand.
notes: About 0.39 %; straight flushes are excluded.

name: Probability of a Straight Flush (5-Card Poker)
description: Gives the chance of a straight flush, including a royal flush, in five cards.
notes: About 1 in 65,000; a royal flush alone is 4 in 2,598,960.

name: Probability of a Pocket Pair (Texas Hold'em)
description: Gives the chance that your two private cards form a pair.
notes: About 1 in 17.

name: Number of Triangles in a Triangular Grid

variables.label: Side length n (small triangles per side)

description: Counts all triangles, pointing up or down, in a triangle subdivided into n rows.
notes: A side of 4 contains 27 triangles.

name: Probability of a Total with Three Dice
description: Gives the probability that three fair dice add up to s (Galileo's dice problem).
notes: 10 and 11 are the most likely totals (27/216 each).

name: Expected Number of Dice Rolls to See Every Face
description: Gives the average number of rolls of a fair die needed to see all six faces.
notes: About 14.7 rolls.

name: Probability of No Repeat in n Draws (With Replacement)
description: Gives the chance that n draws with replacement from m equally likely values are all different.
notes: Four random digits are all different 50.4 % of the time.

name: Probability of Exactly k Heads in n Fair Tosses
description: Gives the chance of exactly k heads in n tosses of a fair coin.
notes: Exactly 5 heads in 10 tosses happens only 24.6 % of the time.

name: Longest Run of Heads: Expected Length
description: Approximates the expected length of the longest run of heads in n fair tosses (Schilling 1990).
notes: People faking random sequences usually make runs too short.

name: Probability of a Royal Flush (5-Card Poker)
description: Gives the chance of being dealt A-K-Q-J-10 of one suit in five cards: 4 of the 2,598,960 hands.
notes: About 1 in 649,740.

name: Probability of Completing a Draw with Two Cards to Come
description: Gives the chance of hitting at least one of your "outs" on the turn or river in Texas Hold'em.
notes: A flush draw (9 outs) completes about 35 % of the time; the "rule of 4" gives 36 %.
